brief_item.title: VulnGym拆解仓库级漏洞定位与证据构建
brief_item.core_conclusion: VulnGym把漏洞检测拆成仓库探索、入口定位、关键操作和证据轨迹，避免测预选函数。184份公告、408条条目中，Hard端到端ES仅11.63%，定位失败占失败56.5%。
brief_item.mechanism: 每条记录绑定脆弱版本仓库快照、行级EP、CO和有序trace；T1要求完整探索与证据，T2至T4用oracle分别测入口、关键操作和轨迹构建。评测使用只读cat、rg、sed等命令。
brief_item.result: Hard案例中DeepSeek-V4-Flash+OpenHands达到AR22.58%、ER15.22%、ES11.63%；Qwen3.5-27B+Claude Code为12.90%、8.70%、4.55%。给定入口后，trace ES为36.37%。
brief_item.boundary: 这是只读漏洞检测基准，不等于生产安全或编码成功；覆盖23仓库，结果受模型与scaffold影响。未证明索引能减少工具调用或时延。
brief_item.project_relevance: 可用oracle分解诊断Agent瓶颈是Read/Grep导航、定位还是证据构建，决定是否引入仓库索引。验收记录定位准确率、证据完整性、token和端到端时延。

facts.title: VulnGym: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Repository-Level Vulnerability Detection
facts.event_hint: arXiv:2608.02001v1 introduces a trace-annotated repository-level vulnerability benchmark for coding agents
facts.problem: Most vulnerability benchmarks classify preselected functions and lack line-level execution traces, so they do not test whether a coding agent can explore a repository, locate the relevant entry point and critical operation, and construct evidence for the full vulnerability path.
facts.mechanism: VulnGym aligns reviewed GitHub advisories with vulnerable-version repository snapshots. Each entry is annotated with line-level entry points (EP), critical operations (CO), and ordered vulnerability traces. It defines one end-to-end task (T1) that requires repository exploration, detection, and supporting evidence, plus three oracle-conditioned tasks: entry-point identification (T2), critical-operation localization (T3), and trace construction (T4). This decomposition separates search/localization failures from evidence-construction failures. The study evaluates read-only coding-agent scaffolds including Claude Code, OpenHands, and MiniSWE with multiple LLMs.

evidence.claim: VulnGym contains 184 reviewed advisories and 408 vulnerability entries across 23 open-source repositories, each with line-level entry points, critical operations, and vulnerability traces.
evidence.condition: Entries are aligned to vulnerable repository versions and annotated with fine-grained code evidence.
evidence.source_locator: PDF pp.1-2, Abstract and benchmark contributions

evidence.claim: On Hard cases, the best evaluated frontier configuration (DeepSeek-V4-Flash with OpenHands) achieved 22.58% AR, 15.22% ER, and 11.63% ES, while Qwen3.5-27B with Claude Code achieved 12.90%, 8.70%, and 4.55% respectively.
evidence.condition: End-to-end T1 over Hard vulnerability entries; AR/ER/ES are the paper's reported detection metrics.
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.6, Table 2 and Frontier Coding Agents on Hard Cases

evidence.claim: For Qwen3.5-9B with Claude Code, end-to-end AR/ER/ES declined from 6.36%/4.32%/2.52% on Easy to 3.23%/1.79%/1.67% on Medium and all reached zero on Hard; even Qwen3.5-27B achieved only 12.90%/8.70%/4.55% on Hard.
evidence.condition: Difficulty stratified by trace length; Easy ≤7, Medium =8, Hard ≥9.
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.6, Model Scaling across Difficulty Levels

evidence.claim: With oracle entry-point/critical-operation pairs, the strongest trace-construction ES was 36.37%, while trace-node recall TNR ranged 30.60%-53.96% and precision TNP 14.61%-26.71% across agents.
evidence.condition: Oracle-conditioned T4 on Hard cases; endpoint uncertainty removed.

evidence.claim: Among 347 relation-level T1 failures on Hard, 26.8% had no endpoint file match and 29.7% reached a correct file but not the correct line; together these localization failures accounted for 56.5% of failures.
evidence.condition: Failure composition over the Hard T1 relation-level outputs.

facts.evaluation_context: The benchmark evaluates repository-level vulnerability detection with read-only commands (cat, find, grep, head, ls, nl, pwd, rg, sed, tail, wc). Models include Qwen3.5-2B/4B/9B/27B plus DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MiniMax-M3, and GLM-5.2; scaffolds include Claude Code, OpenHands, and MiniSWE. Entries are stratified by trace length into Easy/Medium/Hard, and T1 is complemented by oracle-conditioned localization and trace tasks. Practical analysis compares per-run tokens and cost with detection performance.
facts.limitations: VulnGym measures vulnerability detection and evidence construction, not general coding-agent task success or production security incident prevention. Hard-case results remain low even for the strongest evaluated configuration, and scaffold/LLM compatibility materially changes outcomes. The benchmark covers 23 repositories and a finite set of reviewed advisories, so repository and CWE distribution, contamination, and generalization require separate validation. Read-only tool restrictions differ from unrestricted production agents; the paper reports token/cost trade-offs but no universal latency, energy, or deployment-throughput guarantee.
facts.project_relevance: This benchmark directly exposes the cost and failure modes of repository exploration: agents must search, read, localize line-level endpoints, and assemble evidence traces rather than classify a preselected function. Its oracle decomposition can diagnose whether an agent's bottleneck is Read/Grep navigation, endpoint localization, or trace construction; however, it does not itself provide an acceleration technique or prove that a repository index reduces tool calls or latency.
source_notes: Primary arXiv PDF was fetched and the title matches the input metadata exactly.
Metric abbreviations (AR, ER, ES, FR, LR, FP, TNR, TNP) are retained as reported; no alternate interpretation was added.
